name: RAG Chunking Visualizer
contribution: A neobrutalist learning lab that shows how RAG chunk size and overlap help or hurt retrieval.
headline: See your chunks before they break your RAG pipeline
summary: RAG Chunking Visualizer is a single-file, client-side tool built for vibe coders and learners who want to understand retrieval config without spinning up a backend. Upload or paste text, drag chunk and overlap sliders, and watch health warnings, pipeline strips, and a live chunk grid update in real time—including overlap highlights, cut maps, and preset comparisons inspired by real-world Broken, Fragmented, Redundant, and Optimal strategies.
body:
Most RAG tutorials tell you to pick a chunk size and hope for the best. This project makes the tradeoffs visible: zero overlap slices sentences apart, tiny chunks fragment meaning, and greedy overlap burns tokens on duplicate context.

Middle Out Consulting built the visualizer as a Cafe Cursor Brisbane demo—a neobrutalist split-pane learn mode with guided lessons, a "How this works" tour, light and dark themes, and a high-contrast mode for readability. Everything runs in the browser: import documents, export configs, share settings via URL hash, and compare strategies side by side.

The goal is simple: cause (your sliders) and effect (chunks on screen) stay together so you can tune retrieval with confidence before you wire LangChain or LlamaIndex into production.
